overall: The AG found the committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to create and approve minutes from July 2010 to January 2012, and ordered compliance and retroactive minutes; meeting-time and 48-hour notice complaints were rejected.

allegations.summary: The committee allegedly failed to create and approve minutes of its meetings for at least two years, from July 2010 through January 2012.
The complainant alleged the committee holds meetings at times difficult for members of the public to attend.
allegations.key_passage: While we encourage the Committee to meet at times that are convenient for both the public and members of the Committee, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law in either regard.

allegations.summary: The complainant alleged the committee posts meeting notices barely more than 48 hours before meetings.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law in either regard.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Create and approve minutes of all Committee meetings dating back to July 1, 2010, to the best of its ability, within 90 days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: In addition to the remedial steps proposed by the Committee, we order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and order the Committee to create and approve minutes of all Committee meetings dating back to July 1, 2010, to the best of its ability.
